scope: Source-first assistant annotations, frozen before API verification; not independent human expert gold. Tests conditional retention of relation skeletons with scheme/commitment unspecified, not final scheme accuracy or end-to-end extraction coverage. Negative probes control trivial acceptance.

references.source_reading: The effective public-health plan supports the favorable evaluation.
Propaganda and misinformation are reasons not to listen.
Lack of human-rights expertise is an offered reason to distrust the officials.
Loss of control and anarchy/death justify not praising the actions.
Historical land theft motivates hesitation about unconditional returns.
The dentist anecdote is offered as additional evidence of growing public sentiment.
Memorials and historical movies illustrate the broader human tendency to remember.
Nature knowing best is offered as a basis for approving environmental help.
Historical self-provision/tradition supports rejecting dependence on food aid.
Reliance on others is projected to impair future self-provision.
Honorable past leaders oppose wholesale rejection of time-tested methods.
The leadership example is explicitly offered as proof that traditional and modern elements can blend.
Cultural inheritance explicitly justifies fighting for preservation.
The general duty to protect cultural heritage supports this preservation judgment.
Persistent leadership/systemic oppression motivates the need for work beyond removing Putin.
Presence of women and children is offered as a reason to infer men are also present.
Poverty and violence instantiate the claimed worse problems.
The more serious problems justify shifting attention to them.
Comparison of local disruptions with wider environmental catastrophe supports the final priority recommendation.
The German example is offered to support Brazil being able to address multiple issues.
Capacity to multitask is a reason to criticize the single-priority view.
Shutdowns in the named countries are the basis for the possibility of wider shutdowns.
Previous experiences of similar groups motivate the expectation about Myanmar.
Working with China against citizens supports the claim of alignment with China.
Distinct political contexts motivate impartial assessment.
Country differences justify calling the worldwide generalization hasty.
Freedom of speech is explicitly given as a reason censorship is dangerous.
Risk of limiting controversial speech supports rejecting government control over who is right.
Allowing invasive species is projected to threaten more than the local ecosystem.
The hypothetical ecosystem collapse is projected to hurt pollinators.
The hypothetical food-production hit is projected to produce food shortage.
The counterfactual failure to resign is projected as possibly leading to poor decisions.
The current author evaluation is not offered as a reason for Biden having commended China.
An established Australian relationship is not projected to cause a dentist conversation.
The source does not reverse the dependency warning into incapacity causing the initial reliance.
The right to fight is not offered as evidence establishing cultural inheritance.
The recommendation to focus is not offered as proof of poverty and violence.
Brazilian choices are not forecast to produce German multitasking.
The source does not reverse the production-to-shortage conditional.
Poor decisions are not presented as causing the counterfactual non-resignation.

representation_and_ambiguity_limits.issue: Central majority-as-justification is embedded within unit0; repeating the position in unit3 is not automatically a distinct inference.
The central majority-choice justification is internal to unit3; the separate land-theft relation does not cover that central warrant.
Organic/natural conditions and gradual preference are clear content, but a qualification is not automatically evidential support; no unambiguous inter-unit support reference assigned.
The exhaustive choice is internal to unit0 and restated in2; repetition is not automatically an offered premise-to-conclusion link.
